transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, what scared me enough to actually make the appointment is... I just keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up. And lately, sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic, I'll catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the steering wheel. It really frightened me to realize I was thinking like that, so that's why I'm here today.
When you imagine not turning the steering wheel, do you feel that you might actually do it?

I don't know... and I think that's exactly why it scared me so much. Like I said, I just catch myself staring at the road after leaving the clinic, and the urge is just... there. I haven't done it, obviously, but I worry that in a split second I might actually just let it happen. It just keeps feeling like it would be so much easier to not have to wake up and do it all again tomorrow.
Do you currently intend to make your car leave the road or otherwise act on these thoughts?

No, I don't intend to. I don't have a plan to do it or anything. It's just... like I said, I keep having these thoughts that it would be easier if I didn't wake up. And then the driving thing... it's more of a wondering what would happen if I didn't turn the wheel, rather than a plan to actually do it. But the fact that my mind even goes there is what scared me enough to come see you.
Have you ever had a distinct period when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable compared with your normal self?

Yes, actually. Earlier this month, I had a period where I felt almost... electrically upbeat, I guess you could say. But then it turned into me just snapping at everyone over really tiny things. Like, at the clinic, if someone misplaced a medication cup or if there was a slight change in our morning schedule, I would just lose my temper with them. It really didn't feel like my usual self at all.
How long did that unusually upbeat or irritable period last?
I'm not exactly sure how long it lasted. I didn't really track the days. It was just a stretch of time earlier this month where I felt that way, but I couldn't give you an exact number of days.
During that unusually upbeat or irritable period, did you need less sleep than usual while still feeling rested?

Yes, actually. During that high-energy stretch, I was sleeping maybe three hours a night. I'd still get up before sunrise feeling completely sharp. I was just convinced I didn't really need any more rest than that.
About how many days did that unusually upbeat or irritable period last?

Like I mentioned a minute ago, I really don't have an exact number for you. I wasn't keeping track of the days on a calendar or anything while it was happening. It was just a stretch of time earlier this month. I'm sorry, I just don't know exactly how long it was.
Did that unusually upbeat or irritable period last at least four days in a row?

I... I really couldn't say for sure if it was four days in a row. I know you're looking for a specific timeframe, but like I was saying, I just wasn't paying attention to the calendar. It could have been four days, or maybe more, but... I honestly just don't know for certain.
How much did that unusually energized or irritable period interfere with your ability to function at work?

Well, it interfered a lot. I’ve actually started making mistakes at the clinic, which really isn't like me. And it spills over into everything else, too. I’m avoiding my friends right now because... well, I’m afraid I’ll either snap at someone or just completely fall apart. 

It's affecting my whole life, honestly. At home, my husband has had to take over basically everything. He's doing the bills, making the meals... and he's having to keep an eye on me to keep me safe when the thoughts get dark. So, yes, it's been very hard to function.
During that unusually energized period, did your thoughts feel unusually fast or difficult to keep up with?

No, I wouldn't say so. My mind wasn't really racing or... hard to keep up with, no. I mean, I had all that energy and irritability, but my thoughts themselves were moving at a pretty normal speed, I think. So, no, I didn't experience that.
During that energized or irritable period, did you become noticeably more active or take on more projects than usual?

Yes, I did. I actually took on a lot more than usual. I picked up extra shifts at the clinic, and then at home, I just... I completely redid our entire household care schedule. I started contacting contractors for things around the house, and I was trying to coordinate everyone's tasks like I was managing a major hospital project. And the thing is, no one had even asked me to take all of that on. I just did it.
Did you ever need to be hospitalized because of that unusually energized or irritable period?

No, I didn't. I've never had to go to the hospital for... for being energized or irritable like that. Like I mentioned, my husband was watching me pretty closely at home, but it never got to the point where I needed to be admitted. So, no.
Was there any stretch of at least seven days in a row when you felt unusually energized or irritable like that?
No, it wasn't a full week. I know it lasted for a few days, maybe three or four days in a row where I was just going non-stop with the house and the clinic, but it definitely wasn't seven days.
How long have you been feeling persistently depressed or hopeless?
Well, the depression has been hanging over me for... gosh, about 11 months now. It's been there a long time, even before this past month made everything just feel completely unbearable.
During these 11 months of depression, have you lost interest or pleasure in most of the things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I really have. I haven't even touched my camera in... a long time. I haven't checked the bird feeders with any real interest, or cared at all about what's coming up in the garden. It's actually really frightening, because those things used to be how I felt like myself. Now I just have no interest in them whatsoever.
Did your husband or anyone at the clinic comment that you seemed noticeably different—more energized or irritable than usual—during that period?

No, I don't think so. My husband didn't say anything to me about it. And no one at the clinic mentioned that I seemed different or irritable, either. I mean, if they did notice anything unusual about how I was acting, they didn't bring it up to me.
Before this recent energized period, have you ever had another distinct stretch of several days when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I don't think so. I can't recall any other time where I felt like that for days on end, or where I didn't need to sleep. This recent time was the only one I can think of.
During that energized period, were you still feeling depressed and uninterested in things, or did your mood and interest noticeably improve?

Um, no, I wasn't feeling depressed then. It was actually the opposite. My mood definitely improved, and I had all that energy, so I wasn't feeling down or uninterested like I had been. It was just a complete shift from how I'd been feeling before.
Looking back, did that unusually energized or irritable state continue for four full days in a row?

I'm honestly not sure. I mean, I wasn't really keeping track of the exact time while it was happening. It was definitely a stretch of a few days, but... I couldn't tell you for certain if it was exactly four full days in a row.
During that energized period specifically, did your mood and behavior cause marked impairment in your ability to work or manage daily life?

No, I wouldn't say it caused any real problems. Um, I was still going to work at the clinic and doing my job just fine. If anything, I felt like I was getting a lot more done than usual because I had all that extra energy. It didn't really get in the way of my daily life at all.
